facts.statement: The genus Synechodus was described by Woodward in 1888.
Synechodus is known from 16 species that lived primarily from the Late Triassic to the Paleocene.
facts.quote: It is known from 16 species primarily spanning from the Late Triassic to Paleocene.

facts.statement: Synechodus had multicusped teeth used for grasping.
facts.quote: The dentition is multicusped and was used for grasping.

facts.statement: Skeletal remains of Synechodus dubrisiensis are known from the Cretaceous of Europe.
facts.quote: Skeletal remains are also known of the species Synechodus dubrisiensis from the Cretaceous of Europe.

facts.statement: A skeleton of an indeterminate Synechodus species from the Early Cretaceous (Albian) of France had a body length of around 70 cm.
facts.quote: A skeleton of an indeterminate species is also known from the Early Cretaceous (Albian) of France, with a body length of around 70 cm.

facts.statement: The oldest known Synecodontiformes from the Early Permian of Russia were assigned to the genus as Synechodus antiquus, though this attribution is debated by other authors.
facts.quote: The remains of the oldest known Synecodontiformes from the Early Permian of Russia have been assigned to the genus as the species Synechodus antiquus, though other authors have considered its attribution to the genus doubtful, with other authors considering attribution of all other pre-Jurassic species to genus being questionable.

facts.statement: The time range for Synechodus is from the Sakmarian to the Lutetian (293.52 to 41.03 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Sakmarian to Lutetian (293.52 to 41.03 million years ago)

facts.statement: Synechodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
